extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers, applicants, program officers, and scientific review officers involved in NIAID/NIH research grant review
extracted.subtask_description: Standard review criteria and SOP guidance for NIH/NIAID peer reviewers to assess the scientific and technical merit of research project grant applications (e.g., R01 and other mechanisms), plus procedures for initiative-specific criteria, human subjects, animals, and special application types. Notes the upcoming Simplified Peer Review Framework effective Jan 25, 2025.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall impact score
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers give applications an overall impact score after considering the review criteria. An overall impact score reflects their assessment of the project’s likelihood to exert a sustained, powerful influence on its field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The overall impact score is based on the committee's judgment after considering all specified review criteria (and any initiative‑specific criteria incorporated into them).

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project address an important problem or a critical barrier to progress in the field? Is the prior research that serves as the key support for the proposed project rigorous? If the aims of the project are achieved, how will scientific knowledge, technical capability, and/or clinical practice be improved? How will successful completion of the aims change the concepts, methods, technologies, treatments, services, or preventative interventions that drive this field?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess importance of the problem, rigor of supporting prior research, and the potential for the project to advance knowledge, practice, or technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the program director(s)/principal investigator(s) (PDs/PIs), collaborators, and other researchers well suited to the project? If early-stage investigators or those in the early stages of independent careers, do they have appropriate experience and training? If established, have they demonstrated an ongoing record of accomplishments that have advanced their field(s)? If the project is collaborative or multi-PD/PI, do the investigators have complementary and integrated expertise; are their leadership approach, governance, and organizational structure appropriate for the project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider qualifications, track record, suitability for the scope/stage of the project, and adequacy of leadership and team integration for multi‑PI efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the application challenge and seek to shift current research or clinical practice paradigms by utilizing novel theoretical concepts, approaches or methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions? Are the concepts, approaches or methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions novel to one field of research or novel in a broad sense? Is a refinement, improvement, or new application of theoretical concepts, approaches or methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions proposed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge both truly paradigm-shifting novelty and meaningful refinements or new applications of existing concepts/techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the overall strategy, methodology, and analyses well-reasoned and appropriate to accomplish the Specific Aims of the project? Have the investigators included plans to address weaknesses in the rigor of prior research that serves as the key support for the proposed project? Have the investigators presented strategies to ensure a robust and unbiased approach, as appropriate for the work proposed? Are potential problems, alternative strategies, and benchmarks for success presented? If the project is in the early stages of development, will the strategy establish feasibility and will particularly risky aspects be managed? Have the investigators presented adequate plans to address relevant biological variables, such as sex, for studies in vertebrate animals or human subjects?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess methodological rigor, plans to address prior weaknesses, mitigation of bias, contingency plans, benchmarks, feasibility for early-stage work, and attention to relevant biological variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach — human subjects and clinical research plans
rubrics_metrics.description: If the project involves human subjects and/or NIH-defined clinical research, are the plans to address 1) protection of human subjects from research risks, and 2) inclusion (or exclusion) of individuals on the basis of sex, race, and ethnicity as well as the inclusion (or exclusion) of individuals of all ages (including children and older adults) justified in terms of the scientific goals and research strategy proposed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When human subjects/clinical research is involved, justification for protections and inclusion/exclusion decisions must be evaluated as part of the Approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the scientific environment in which the work will be done contribute to the probability of success? Are the institutional support, equipment, and other physical resources available to the investigators adequate for the project proposed? Will the project benefit from unique features of the scientific environment, subject populations, or collaborative arrangements?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider institutional support, available equipment/resources, unique environment features, and access to appropriate subject populations or collaborations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: For most research grant and mentored career development award applications, NIH instructs reviewers to assess the project's rigor and transparency, as addressed by questions in the Significance and Approach sections. For institutional training grants, institutional and individual career development awards, and individual fellowships, applicants are required to include a plan for formal instruction in rigorous experimental design and transparency to enhance reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate plans and evidence addressing rigor, reproducibility, and transparency (and for training grants, presence of formal instruction plans). See 'Enhancing Reproducibility Through Rigor and Transparency' for additional guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for human subjects (non-exempt research)
rubrics_metrics.description: For research that involves human subjects but does not involve one of the categories of research that are exempt under 45 CFR Part 46, the committee will evaluate the justification for involvement of human subjects and the proposed protections from research risk relating to their participation according to the following five review criteria: 1) risk to subjects, 2) adequacy of protection against risks, 3) potential benefits to the subjects and others, 4) importance of the knowledge to be gained, and 5) data and safety monitoring for clinical trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should explicitly judge each of these five elements for non-exempt human subjects research and consult SF 424 Application Guides and supplemental reviewer guidance as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for human subjects (exempt research)
rubrics_metrics.description: For research that involves human subjects and meets the criteria for one or more of the eight categories of research that are exempt under 45 CFR Part 46, the committee will evaluate: 1) the justification for the exemption, 2) human subjects involvement and characteristics, and 3) sources of materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even for exempt categories, reviewers must ensure the exemption is justified and evaluate nature of involvement/characteristics and sources of materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of women, minorities, and individuals across the lifespan
rubrics_metrics.description: When the proposed project involves human subjects and/or NIH-defined clinical research, reviewers assess the adequacy of plans to include (or exclude) on the basis of sex, race, and ethnicity as well as the inclusion (or exclusion) of individuals of all ages, as appropriate, for the scientific goals of the research. Reviewers will also evaluate plans for recruiting and retaining subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the scientific justification for inclusion/exclusion across demographics and the feasibility/plans for recruitment and retention. Note NIH's child definition change (under 18 now). See SF 424 Application Guides and Guidelines for the Review of Inclusion for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate animals
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee will evaluate the involvement of live vertebrate animals as part of the scientific assessment according to the following criteria: 1) description of proposed procedures involving animals, including species, strains, ages, sex, and total number to be used; 2) justifications for the use of animals versus alternative models and for the appropriateness of the species proposed; and 3) interventions to minimize discomfort, distress, pain and injury to that which is unavoidable in the conduct of scientifically sound research including the use of analgesic, anesthetic, tranquilizing drugs, or comfortably restraining devices; and 4) justification for euthanasia method if NOT consistent with American Veterinary Medical Association Guidelines for the Euthanasia of Animals guidelines, you will need to describe and scientifically justify your methods on the Cover Page Supplement form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should ensure detailed description, justification for animal use/species, plans to minimize suffering, and justification for any non‑standard euthanasia methods. See SF 424 Application Guides and Worksheet for Applications Involving Animals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess whether materials or procedures proposed are potentially hazardous to research personnel and/or the environment, and if needed, determine whether adequate protection is proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider biosafety risks and adequacy of proposed protections/containment procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewing a resubmission application, the committee will evaluate the application as now presented, taking into consideration the responses to comments from the previous scientific review group and changes made to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether prior reviewer concerns were adequately addressed and whether revisions strengthen the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewing a renewal application, the committee will consider the progress made in the last funding period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate documented accomplishments/progress and whether continued funding is justified based on prior results and future plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewing a revision application, the committee will consider the appropriateness of the proposed expansion of the scope of the project. If the revision application relates to investigation in the original application that was not recommended for approval, the committee will consider whether the responses to comments from the previous scientific review group are adequate and whether substantial changes are clearly evident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the scope expansion is appropriate and whether prior critiques were adequately addressed when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplified Peer Review Framework (Jan 25, 2025)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications due on or after January 25, 2025, NIH will use the Simplified Peer Review Framework to score most research project grant applications. Notably, the new Framework reorganizes the five regulatory criteria (Significance, Investigators, Innovation, Approach, Environment) into three factors (Importance of the Research, Rigor and Feasibility, and Expertise and Resources).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This SOP notes that for many applications the standard five criteria will be replaced by the simplified three-factor framework; reviewers and applicants should consult relevant NIH guidance for details on scoring and factor definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiative-specific / additional review criteria guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Other investigator-initiated application types and initiatives (e.g., P01, R34, U01, RFAs, PARs) may include additional review criteria in the notice of funding opportunity. These additional criteria should be incorporated into the five core criteria so they can be captured in the Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing RFAs/PARs, use the investigator-initiated review criteria template; if additional criteria are necessary, develop them with the scientific review officer and incorporate them into core criteria because additional criteria cannot be recorded separately in the Commons. For standard program announcements, you cannot include additional review criteria or expand standard review criteria.
